title: What lightning does to your body ⚡
subject: lightning
description:
Would you go outside in a storm now? 👇

What happens if you get struck by lightning? Air near a bolt heats to about 50,000°F, hotter than the Sun's surface, yet about 90% of people struck survive, though many have long-term effects. In a 2024 lab study on model heads, 92 to 97% of the current flowed over the surface. Some survivors get temporary fern-like marks called Lichtenberg figures. When thunder roars, go indoors.

Sources: National Weather Service ("How Dangerous is Lightning?", Lightning Safety), Scientific Reports (2024, doi:10.1038/s41598-023-50563-w), Frontiers in Medicine (2021) Lichtenberg figure case report, Live Science

scenes.text: Lightning can paint a fern on your skin.
The air around a bolt heats to about 50,000 degrees Fahrenheit, hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Yet about 90% of people struck by lightning survive.
But here's the strange part. In lab tests on model heads, over 90% of the current raced over the outside.
Where it passes, red branching marks called Lichtenberg figures can bloom on the skin.
They often fade within a few days, like a signature the bolt leaves behind.
